44291630.article_content:
An image of two laptops, the one on the left accessing the internet for free and the one on the right having a $60/day connection. The router used to spoof the MAC address is connected to an Anker Zolo power bank.
Table of Contents
The script
Picture this, you’re a teenager in the middle of the ocean on a cruise ship. All is good, except you’re lacking your lifeblood: internet. You could pay $170 for seven days of throttled internet on a
single
device, and perhaps split it via a travel router or hotspot, but that still seems less than ideal.
I’ve been travelling Europe with family and am currently on Princess Cruises’ Sun Princess cruise ship. For the past two days, the ship has mostly been in port, so I was able to use a cellular connection. This quickly became not feasible as we got further from land, where there was no coverage. At around the same time, I wanted to download the Princess Cruises app on my phone, and realized that it would give me a
one-time 15-minute
internet connection. I activated it, and quickly realized that it didn’t limit you to just the Play Store or App Store: all websites could be accessed. I soon realized that this “one-time” download was MAC-address dependent and thus, could be bypassed by switching MAC addresses. However, doing so logs you out of the MedallionNet portal, which is required to get the 15-minutes of free internet.
This means that in order to get just 15 minutes of internet, the following is required:
Change MAC address
Login to MedallionNet with date-of-birth and room number, binding the MAC address to your identity
Send a request with your booking ID activating 15 minutes of free internet, intended to be used for downloading the Princess app
Not completely sure, but it did initially seem that to activate unrestricted access to the internet, you would need to send a simple HTTP to play.google.com, although I don’t think this is needed.
This process, on the surface, seems extremely arduous. But if this could be automated, it would suddenly become a much more viable proposition. After looking at the fetch requests the MedallionNet portal was sending to login and activate the free sessions, I realized that it shouldn’t be
too
hard to automate.
Conveniently, my family also brought a travel router running OpenWRT as we were planning on purchasing the throttled single-device plan (which is ~$170 for the entire cruise) and using the router as a hotspot so we could connect multiple devices to the internet. This router (a GL.iNet) allows you to change the MAC address via the admin portal, needing only a single POST request. This meant that if I could string together the API requests to change the MAC address (after getting a token from the router login endpoint), login to MedallionNet, and request the free internet session, I would have free internet.
I first tried copying the requests as cURL commands via DevTools into Notepad and using a local LLM to vibe-code a simple bash file. Realizing this wasn’t going to work, I began work on a Python script instead. I converted the cURL commands to
requests
via Copilot (yes, I used LLMs to an extent when building this) and started chaining together the requests.
The only issues I faced that took some time to overcome were figuring out how to repeat the requests when needed and being resistant to unexpected HTTP errors. For the former, I initially tried repeating it on an interval (first through a
while True
loop and later via shell scripting in the container) but later realized it was much easier by checking if internet access expired by sending a request to example.com and checking if it fails. For the latter, I used
while True
loops to allow the requests to be retried and executed
break
when the requests succeeded. The only other issue, that still exists, is that occasionally, the connection will drop out while the session is refreshed, although this seems to happen less than every 15 minutes and only lasts for a minute or two.
The container running in Docker Desktop, refreshing the session when needed
After comparing speeds with another guy I met on the cruise (who also happens to be a high-school programmer), who had the highest-level MedallionNet plan, there seems to be no additional throttling (7+ Mbps). Even better, after connecting my power bank’s integrated USB-C cable to the router, I’m able to move around the ship for hours. So far, I’ve been using the router for nearly ~7 hours and my 10,000 mAh power bank is still at 42% battery. In fact, I’m writing this very post while connected to the router.
The script
#
Here’s the code that I’ve been using and a sample .env, although I have a
repository
with the Dockerfile and compose file as well. Also, I’m aware the code isn’t
pretty
, I mostly just wrote it as a proof-of-concept that turned out to work amazingly well. I also doubt I’ll update the code after my cruise ends, since it won’t really be possible to test it. If you try to use this later, and it’s broken, you can go

data.title: If the moon were only 1 pixel: A tediously accurate solar system model (2014)
data.author: sdoering
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要描述了太阳系中各行星之间的巨大距离，强调太空中的 vast 空旷。文章以从地球到火星的旅程为例，说明行星间距离遥远，需要大约七个月的太空旅行才能到达。文章还提到，大多数空间图并未按实际比例绘制，因为太空中的大部分区域都是空旷的。这种空旷超出了人类的直观理解，即使使用比喻或模型也难以准确描述。文章最后反思了人类大脑在处理如此巨大尺度和空无时的局限性，指出我们对宇宙的许多方面难以真正理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“如果月亮只有1像素”的太阳系比例可视化及其相关讨论，包括对宇宙广阔空间的感受、技术实现和类似体验。

不同观点：
• **amelius** 认为光速非常慢，探索其他恒星需要很长时间，可能在拥有全息甲板之前都无法实现。
• **amiga386** 关注HTML/CSS的简单实现，特别是绝对定位和大left值的使用。
• **andersco** 强调这是一种非凡的体验，并提到之前在Hacker News上的讨论。
• **tomxor** 提供了一个192字节的精确太阳系可视化链接，展示了准确的轨道和恒星周期。
• **technothrasher** 分享了小学时使用 vinyl roll 来展示地球历史的类似体验。
• **susam** 提到过去用POV-Ray绘制太阳系行星比例的经验，并讨论了投影方式对视觉效果的影响。
• **robin_reala** 强调光速切换让人感受到宇宙的空旷，等待时间让人深刻理解地球到太阳的距离。
• **jethkl** 提到现实中的太阳系比例模型，并推荐了一些可以步行或骑行的地点。
• **computator** 通过计算说明行星在如此大的比例下仍然可见的奇妙之处。
• **CapsAdmin** 表示尽管看过很多关于宇宙大小的类比，但这次体验尤其震撼，特别是光速的缓慢感。
• **j_m_b** 推荐了Stephen Hawking的Genius中的太阳系比例可视化，并称赞了整个系列。
• **kennu** 抱怨用鼠标滚轮滚动几十万公里太费力，最终放弃了。
• **Symmetry** 指出水星只有1像素大小，并提供了一个照片大小比较的链接。
• **gary17the** 开玩笑说，面对如此广阔的宇宙，如何看待30年还清房贷的问题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到光速和等待时间，这是体验中的一个重要感受点。
• 不同的技术实现和可视化方法被分享，包括HTML/CSS、POV-Ray和192字节的Dwitter可视化。
• 现实中的太阳系比例模型也被提及，提供了实际的参考。
• 评论中包含了一些关于宇宙广阔和人类渺小的哲学性思考和幽默。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于体验的实际操作性和感受，例如kennu对滚动操作的抱怨，以及amelius对光速缓慢的感慨。

(we still love you)
That was about 10 million km (6,213,710 mi) just now.
Pretty empty out here.
Here comes our first planet...
As it turns out, things are pretty far apart.
We’ll be coming up on a new planet soon. Sit tight.
Most of space is just space.
Halfway home.
Destination: Mars!
It would take about seven months to travel this distance in a spaceship.
Better be some good in-flight entertainment.
In case you're wondering, you'd need about 2000 feature-length movies to occupy that many waking hours.
Sit back and relax. Jupiter is more than 3 times as far as we just traveled.
When are we gonna be there?
Seriously. When are we gonna be there?
This is where we might at least see some asteroids to wake us up.
Too bad they're all too small to appear on this map.
I spy, with my little eye... something black.
If you were on a road trip, driving at 75mi/hr, it would have taken you over 500 years to get here from earth.
All these distances are just averages, mind you.
The distance between planets really depends on where the two planets are in their orbits around the sun.
So if you're planning on taking a trip to Jupiter, you might want to use a different map.
If you plan it right, you can actually move relatively quickly between planets.
The New Horizons space craft that launched in 2006 only took 13 months to get to Jupiter.
Don't worry. It'll take a lot less than 13 months to scroll there.
Pretty close to Jupiter now.
Sorry. That was a lie before. Now we really are pretty close.
Lots of time to think out here...
Pop the champagne! We just passed 1 billion km.
I guess this is why most maps of the solar system aren't drawn to scale.
It's not hard to draw the planets.
It's the empty space that's a problem.
Most space charts leave out the most significant part – all the space.
We're used to dealing with things at a much smaller scale than this.
When it comes to things like the age of the earth, the number of snowflakes in Siberia, the national debt...
Those things are too much for our brains to handle.
We need to reduce things down to something we can see or experience directly in order to understand them.
We're always trying to come up with metaphors for big numbers. Even so, they never seem to work.
Let's try a few metaphors anyway...
You would need
of these screens lined up side-by-side to show this whole map at once.
If this map was printed from a quality printer (300 pixels per inch) the earth would be invisible, and the width of the paper would need to be 475 feet.
475 feet is about 1 and 1/2 football fields.
Even though we don’t really understand them, a lot can happen within these massive lengths of time and space.
A drop of water can carve out a canyon.
An amoeba can become a dolphin.
A star can collapse on itself.
It’s easy to disregard nothingness because there’s no thought available to encapsulate it. There’s no metaphor that fits because, by definition, once the nothingness becomes tangible, it ceases to exist.
It’s a good thing we have these tiny stars and planets, otherwise we’d have no point of reference at all.
We’d be surrounded by this stuff that our minds weren’t built to understand.
All this emptiness really could drive you nuts. For instance, if you’re in a sensory deprivation tank for too long, your brain starts to make things up. You see and hear things that aren’t there.
The brain isn't built to handle "empty."
"Sorry, Humanity," says Evolution. "What with all the jaguars trying to eat you, the parasites in your fur, and the never-ending need for a decent steak, I was a little busy. I didn’t exactly have time to come up with a way to conceive of vast stretches of nothingness."
Neurologically speaking, we really only deal with matter of a certain size, and energy of a few select wavelengths. For everything else, we have to make up mental models and see if they match up to the tiny shreds of hard evidence that actually feel real.
The mental models provided by mathematics are extremely helpful when trying to make sense of these vast distances, but still...
Abstraction is pretty unsatisfying.
When you hear people talk about how, "there’s more to this universe than our minds can conceive of" it's usually a way to get you to go along with a half-baked plot point about UFOs or super-powers in a sci-fi series that you're watching late at night when you can’t get to sleep.
Even when Shakespeare wrote: "There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, Than are dreamt of in your philosophy” – he's basically trying to give us a loophole to make the ghost in the story more believable.
But all this empty space, these things of a massive scale, really are more than our minds can conceive of. The maps and metaphors fail to do them justice.
You look at one tiny dot, then you look for the next tiny dot. Everything in between is inconsequential and fairly boring.
Emptiness is actually ever

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意识的本质及其在构建有意识机器中的作用

不同观点：
• **canadiantim** 认为，意识的核心问题是“ qualia”（如红色的视觉或咖啡的气味）是否是现实的基本组成部分，还是可以进一步分解为更基础的东西。他批评文章在没有提供证据的情况下，假设qualia可以被分解，并认为文章没有真正触及意识作为真实现象的本质，而只是将其视为一种抽象层。
• **talkingtab** 对文章的方法表示怀疑，认为文章没有回答如何实际构建有意识机器的具体问题。他强调了“知道某事”和“能够做某事”之间的区别，并提出复杂自适应系统（如人类）的例子，认为应从这些系统的构造中寻找线索。
• **esafak** 简要介绍了文章中提出的意识层次结构模型，并关注如何评估有机体所属的意识阶段，同时提到IIT（整合信息理论）作为一种可能的方法。他感兴趣的是如何确定有机体在层次结构中的位置和程度。
• **AIorNot** 质疑任何物理理论是否能够解释意识的本质，指出我们只能通过自己的主观体验来描述意识。他认为文章可能只是讨论了产生意识的条件，而不是解释意识本身。
• **disambiguation** 质疑文章中关于“基质独立性”的假设，认为文章没有充分解释或证明这一点，并将此视为理论的弱点。他还将文章的立场与Penrose的量子二元论进行了比较，认为后者提供了更强的因果机制解释。
• **gcanyon** 提出，意识是否是AI的必要目标值得讨论。他认为，意识可能是高智能系统的副产品，但不一定是目标，目标应是完成具体任务，而非刻意追求意识。
• **Barrin92** 对文章的学术价值表示怀疑，认为其内容像是拼凑而成，缺乏实质性贡献，甚至像是一种恶作剧。
• **PunchTornado** 认为文章中的观点并无新意，很多内容已经在Chalmers和Dennett等人的工作中被更深入地讨论过，批评文章像是半抄袭他人的想法。
• **catigula** 认为，任何声称对意识有完全解释的理论都是误导，推荐了泛心论和Russellian monism作为值得关注的理论。他批评IIT和幻觉主义理论与科学方法不符。
• **kypro** 持有一种极端的观点，认为意识只是大脑为了提升感官重要性而产生的“谎言”，并认为如果有机器能够报告其“痛苦”，那么这种意识与人类的意识并无实质性区别。
• **m3kw9** 质疑如何定义和测试意识，这是一个关键的争议点。
• **briian** 提出，如果对大脑有更好的理解，是否能够更好地模仿意识，并认为这是解锁LLMs（大型语言模型）更多潜力的关键。

补充讨论：
• 意识是否是构建智能机器的必要条件或副产品是一个重要的讨论点，涉及到对意识本质和实用性的不同看法。
• 关于文章中提出的意识层次结构模型，讨论集中在如何评估和验证有机体在层次结构中的位置，以及是否存在更有效的评估方法如IIT。
• 基质独立性和物理理论在解释意识方面的局限性也是一个重要的争议点，特别是与Penrose的量子二元论的比较。
• 对文章的学术价值和原创性的质疑反映了学术界对跨学科理论构建的严格要求。

data.article_summary: Chawan TUI浏览器发布了0.2.0版本，提供了源代码压缩包和amd64 Linux的静态二进制发行版。安装静态二进制版需解压并以root身份运行"make install"，卸载则运行"make uninstall"。该版本还提供了.deb包。运行时必需的依赖包括libssh2、libbrotli、OpenSSL或LibreSSL。某些旧依赖如zlib、libseccomp等已不再需要。当前版本已具备最小可行产品的所有功能，后续v0.2分支仅修复漏洞，新功能开发将在master分支进行，下个版本计划改进布局模块性能和用户界面友好性。

44293260.article_content:
#
Chawan 0.2.0
Version 0.2.0 of the Chawan TUI browser has been released.
A tarball of the source tree is available
here
.  Please refer to the README
file for compilation instructions.
A static binary distribution for
amd64 Linux
also exists.
To install it, extract the archive somewhere and run
make install
as root.  (To uninstall, run
make uninstall
.)
The same distribution is also available as a
.deb
package
.
##
Information for package maintainers
The current list of mandatory runtime dependencies is:
libssh2.
libbrotli (more precisely, libbrotlicommon and libbrotlidec).
OpenSSL or LibreSSL.  For OpenSSL, you will want 3.0 or later.
For LibreSSL, the version in OpenBSD 7.7 has been tested.
Previous development versions had other dependencies which no
longer apply, and can be dropped.  In particular, zlib, libseccomp,
termcap/ncurses and libcurl are no longer used.
If you run into an issue while packaging Chawan, please contact me
before trying to patch over it.  Chances are we can solve it upstream.
##
What's next
It took a bit longer than expected, but I finally feel OK putting a
version on this.  It has all features I wanted from an MVP, and no known
fatal bugs.
The v0.2 branch in git will only receive bugfixes.  Further work on new
features will continue on the master branch.
For the next release, I hope to improve upon the layout module's
performance & correctness, and to make the UI somewhat more user
friendly.  Stay tuned :)

data.title: Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，突破了传统Transformer因自注意力机制带来的二次元内存和计算开销限制。该模型结合了状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多尺度卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，实现了近似线性的计算扩展，适用于处理大规模序列数据。该研究为长文本处理提供了一种新的解决方案，显著提升了处理效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于非注意力机制的大语言模型（LLMs）的研究及其性能评估

不同观点：
• albertzeyer：认为该论文提出的方法在实验方面不足，尤其是缺乏对长序列外推、大规模实验等的深入研究。同时指出，虽然自注意力机制的复杂度是O(n^2)，但如果序列长度没有比模型维度大很多，这个复杂度问题并不严重。此外，提到已经有许多研究尝试解决自注意力机制的复杂度问题，如xLSTM和Block-Recurrent Transformers，但该论文未引用这些研究。
• juank10：对非注意力机制的LLM持保留态度，认为在代码、数学、推理和多轮问答任务中，注意力机制仍然是关键。同时推荐了几篇关于非注意力模型的论文（MesaNet、Rodimus、Gated DeltaNet、Mamba2）。
• maxrmk：批评论文中对DeepSeek LLM的描述不准确，指出DeepSeek的架构是公开且有详细文档的。
• yorwba：认为论文结构不清晰，重复解释架构但缺乏关键细节，如“外部检索内存”的梯度计算方法。同时指出论文对DeepSeek LLM的描述显得神秘，而实际上已有相关文献。
• daxfohl：关注LLM按token收费的可持续性问题，尤其是在计算需求呈二次增长的情况下。
• imranq：认为论文在实验支持方面不足，尤其是在真实任务测试和推理等方面。但认为去除注意力机制的想法值得关注。
• ljlolel：希望看到更多的图表和图形来说明实验结果。
• zoklet-enjoyer：虽然不太理解技术细节，但对未来可能性感到兴奋。
• gsf_emergency：提供了一个关于非注意力LLM的GitHub链接。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是论文实验部分的不足，特别是在长序列外推、大规模实验和真实任务测试等方面。
• 另一个争议点是对DeepSeek LLM架构的描述不准确，批评者认为已有文献足够清晰，无需猜测。
• 对非注意力机制LLM的潜力存在不同看法，部分评论者认为注意力机制在某些任务中不可或缺，而其他评论者则认为去除注意力机制的想法值得关注。
• 收费模式和计算成本的可持续性也被提及，反映了技术发展对商业模式的影响。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Breaking Quadratic Barriers: A Non-Attention LLM for Ultra-Long Context Horizons, by Andrew Kiruluta and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a novel non attention based architecture for large language models (LLMs) that efficiently handles very long context windows, on the order of hundreds of thousands to potentially millions of tokens. Unlike traditional Transformer designs, which suffer from quadratic memory and computation overload due to the nature of the self attention mechanism, our model avoids token to token attention entirely. Instead, it combines the following complementary components: State Space blocks (inspired by S4) that learn continuous time convolution kernels and scale near linearly with sequence length, Multi Resolution Convolution layers that capture local context at different dilation levels, a lightweight Recurrent Supervisor to maintain a global hidden state across sequential chunks, and Retrieval Augmented External Memory that stores and retrieves high-level chunk embeddings without reintroducing quadratic operations.

44292601.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种不依赖注意力机制的大语言模型架构，能够高效处理超长上下文，突破了传统Transformer因自注意力机制带来的二次元内存和计算开销限制。该模型结合了状态空间块（State Space blocks）、多尺度卷积层（Multi Resolution Convolution layers）、轻量级递归监督器（Recurrent Supervisor）和检索增强外部记忆（Retrieval Augmented External Memory）等组件，实现了近似线性的计算扩展，适用于处理大规模序列数据。该研究为长文本处理提供了一种新的解决方案，显著提升了处理效率。
44292601.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于非注意力机制的大语言模型（LLMs）的研究及其性能评估

不同观点：
• albertzeyer：认为该论文提出的方法在实验方面不足，尤其是缺乏对长序列外推、大规模实验等的深入研究。同时指出，虽然自注意力机制的复杂度是O(n^2)，但如果序列长度没有比模型维度大很多，这个复杂度问题并不严重。此外，提到已经有许多研究尝试解决自注意力机制的复杂度问题，如xLSTM和Block-Recurrent Transformers，但该论文未引用这些研究。
• juank10：对非注意力机制的LLM持保留态度，认为在代码、数学、推理和多轮问答任务中，注意力机制仍然是关键。同时推荐了几篇关于非注意力模型的论文（MesaNet、Rodimus、Gated DeltaNet、Mamba2）。
• maxrmk：批评论文中对DeepSeek LLM的描述不准确，指出DeepSeek的架构是公开且有详细文档的。
• yorwba：认为论文结构不清晰，重复解释架构但缺乏关键细节，如“外部检索内存”的梯度计算方法。同时指出论文对DeepSeek LLM的描述显得神秘，而实际上已有相关文献。
• daxfohl：关注LLM按token收费的可持续性问题，尤其是在计算需求呈二次增长的情况下。
• imranq：认为论文在实验支持方面不足，尤其是在真实任务测试和推理等方面。但认为去除注意力机制的想法值得关注。
• ljlolel：希望看到更多的图表和图形来说明实验结果。
• zoklet-enjoyer：虽然不太理解技术细节，但对未来可能性感到兴奋。
• gsf_emergency：提供了一个关于非注意力LLM的GitHub链接。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是论文实验部分的不足，特别是在长序列外推、大规模实验和真实任务测试等方面。
• 另一个争议点是对DeepSeek LLM架构的描述不准确，批评者认为已有文献足够清晰，无需猜测。
• 对非注意力机制LLM的潜力存在不同看法，部分评论者认为注意力机制在某些任务中不可或缺，而其他评论者则认为去除注意力机制的想法值得关注。
• 收费模式和计算成本的可持续性也被提及，反映了技术发展对商业模式的影响。

data.title: Snorting the AGI with Claude Code
data.author: beigebrucewayne
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM（大型语言模型）生成内容及其在软件开发中应用的讨论

不同观点：
• mjrbrennan认为AI生成的总结质量低下，充满空话，不如直接查看代码提交记录来得快而准确，对AI总结的信任度较低。
• blahgeek指出，要求AI解释Rust的借用检查器是一个不好的例子，因为这类数据在AI的训练数据中已经很多，无法展示其真正的能力。
• rbren偏向于围绕LLM无关的开源代理进行脚本编写，认为这项技术正在从根本上改变软件开发，需确保对工作方式的控制。
• jasonthorsness认为终端是LLM的理想接口，可能比自定义IDE集成更受欢迎。
• b0a04gl担心由模型生成描述、测试和样板代码会悄然降低团队的审查标准，建议追踪模型生成代码对长期bug率和回滚模式的影响。
• AstroBen和distortionfield关注的是评论的可读性和博客主题的美观，而非技术内容本身。
• bionhoward对Anthropic的法律条款表示质疑，认为其不合理的条款可能影响其作为AI安全管理者的可信度。
• jvanderbot期待与AI相关的财务投资减少，似乎对AI在软件开发中的角色持保留态度。
• SamPatt和dweinus认为Claude代码的功能强大，特别是在脚本编写方面，能够处理多种任务，但对其价格和准确性存在一定质疑。
• abhisheksp1993对命令行玩笑表示幽默。
• dirtbag__dad对LLM自动化生成变更日志和测试等功能表示赞赏，并询问是否已有类似GitHub actions或pre-commit的工具。
• tinyhouse认为文章内容杂乱，对幻灯片描述代码库的实用性表示怀疑，并指出文中的许多功能并非新颖，且与AGI无关。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对AI生成内容的质量和可信度存在争议，部分人认为不如人工处理可靠。
• LLM在软件开发中的角色和未来应用场景是讨论的焦点，包括其对工作流程的潜在影响和自动化能力的价值。
• 对AI生成内容的长期影响和相关工具的现有实现也有一定讨论。
• 部分评论偏离主题，关注文章的可读性和视觉设计等非技术问题。

data.title: Retrobootstrapping Rust for some reason
data.author: romac
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到用户被随机选中进行CAPTCHA验证以确认请求有效。页面提供了一个登录表单，包括账户名、密码输入框和“记住我”选项。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的选项。用户需完成CAPTCHA验证才能继续。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： reproducing old builds of LLVM and Rust, and the challenges associated with backwards compatibility and bootstrapping in modern compilers.

不同观点：
• **Kimixa** 认为，现代的 clang 和 gcc 无法编译旧版本的 LLVM，主要是由于 C++ 标准的变化。通过在编译选项中指定 "std=xxx" 可以解决此问题。他还提到，自己成功编译了2011年左右的LLVM版本，但遇到了一些LLVM代码中的bug。Kimixa 还指出，C++ 对旧代码的兼容性支持过于僵化，对新版本的发展有负面影响。

• **Jasonthorsness** 对即使在2011年这么近的时间点上重现构建也存在困难感到担忧，并质疑技术是否会稳定下来，还是会变得更糟。他提出了一个更广泛的问题：将来是否会遇到现有技术无法再构建的情况。

• **LegionMammal978** 分享了自己在Ubuntu 20.04上进行类似项目的经验，遇到了LLVM堆栈问题，并且一些提交的哈希在公共repo中找不到。这增加了重建缺失提交的工作量。

• **Tmtvl** 提到Guix在引导Rust时遇到了问题，并引用了一篇2018年的文章。这表明Rust的 bootstrapping 问题在不同的项目中都有出现。

• **Neilv** 提出是否可以创建一个简化的Rust编译器实现，接受最新的Rust语言输入但不做检查，仅用于最小化步骤的可持续引导。他还赞扬了Debian在维护旧软件包方面的成功。

补充讨论：
• **Gregorvand** 和 **fcoury** 提到了访问某些链接时遇到的问题，并提供了替代链接以帮助访问被禁止的内容。

• **Eptcyka** 对Nix evangelists的某些行为提出批评，但承认在重现构建问题时，使用Nix固定nixpkgs版本和源代码可以减轻负担。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于C++和Rust等语言对旧代码的兼容性支持是否合理，以及这种支持是否对语言的现代发展造成了不必要的负担。Kimixa认为这种兼容性过度僵化，而Neilv则在寻找一种简化的编译器实现来解决引导问题。

data.author: ges
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对3D视口工具的体验与反馈，包括技术实现、用户体验（UX）及功能建议。

不同观点：
• [技术实现相关]  
  ◦ [lvncelot] 提到在尝试将 Fabric.js 用于3D视口时遇到很多意外行为，最终选择实现传统的3D操控工具。他们使用了 esm.js 而非 WASM 实现3D引擎，且应用主要针对桌面鼠标用户，而非触控设备。  
  ◦ [Flux159] 对 R3F（React Three Fiber）的体验感兴趣，并询问是否考虑开源。他还提到使用 Fabric.js 管理2D画布对象的经验，并询问该工具是否可以用于创建3D编辑器。

• [UX和界面问题]  
  ◦ [socalgal2] 提到界面缺少“Add”按钮，而界面上的按钮与描述不符。  
  ◦ [WhitneyLand] 指出捏拉缩放（pinch zoom）会导致UX问题，建议如果不想支持双指手势，至少应该禁用以防止干扰体验。  
  ◦ [kookamamie] 认为UX可以改进，提到登陆页面的字幕像出故障了一样，图标看起来“模糊”，并质疑“下一代”的定义。  
  ◦ [guigui] 提到在白色背景上，操控按钮（移动、旋转等）看起来像是被禁用了。  
  ◦ [Bengalilol] 表示无法移动相机，询问是否遗漏了明显的东西。  
  ◦ [Eduard] 提到在Android Chrome上双指输入无效，已放置的对象会“跳出”视口。

data.title: Show HN: Canine – A Heroku alternative built on Kubernetes
data.author: czhu12
data.article_summary: Canine 是一个简化 Kubernetes 集群部署的平台，结合了 Kubernetes 的强大功能和 Heroku 的简洁性。它提供了直观的用户界面，便于管理和部署。主要功能包括：通过 Docker 和 Docker Compose 进行安装和运行，支持自定义端口，以及 Canine Cloud 提供的高级功能如 GitHub 集成、团队协作、实时监控和较低的维护需求。安装可通过一行命令完成，平台还提供了详细的安装说明和云服务选项。项目遵循 Apache-2.0 许可证，目前在 GitHub 上有 729 个星标和 22 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Canine.sh 平台的优缺点、功能、以及与其他类似平台的比较

不同观点：
• [TheTaytay] 对 Canine 平台的文档和功能表示赞赏，但对如何使用和管理 K8s 集群存在疑问，特别是关于集群的构建和管理方式（单机还是多机），以及是否能与现有 K8s 集群集成。
• [bpiroman] 推荐使用 Kamal 并将其部署到 Hetzner 实例上，认为这是一个更简单的选择。
• [debarshi] 提供了一个 PaaS 平台的列表，认为用户可以参考更多选项。
• [czhu12] 分享了自己使用 Canine 搭建整个技术栈的满足感，尤其是从硬件到软件的全栈掌控体验，但这一体验更偏向个人项目和实验性质。
• [nwienert] 对 Canine 的文档中的“为什么不应使用 Canine”部分表示不满，认为 sarcastic 的内容对用户决策没有帮助，建议直接说明使用 Canine 需要面对的实际问题，如服务器管理责任等。

补充讨论：
• [vanillax] 纠正了 Canine 文档中关于 Kubernetes 运行 Docker 容器的说法，指出 Kubernetes 实际上运行的是符合 OCI 标准的容器，"Docker" 只是品牌名称。
• [lotyrin] 提到自己尝试过 Docker 和 Kubernetes，但觉得两者之间缺少一个“甜蜜点”，Canine 是否能真正简化 K8s 的使用尚不明确。
• [stego-tech] 赞赏 Canine 的概念，并计划尝试使用它来替代 Microcloud，但也提到 K8s 的复杂性是其广泛应用的一个障碍。
• [JeffMcCune] 对 Canine 使用 Google Sheets 作为后端表示兴趣，并提到自己曾有类似的创建 Heroku-like 体验的想法，表示愿意探讨与 Canine 的集成可能性。
• [matus_congrady] 提到自己的平台 Stacktape，指出 Canine 面临的挑战，特别是与 Heroku 这样经过多年优化的平台相比，Canine 在开发者体验和功能完整性上可能存在差距，尤其在生产环境中的可靠性和扩展性方面。
• [konexis007] 询问 Canine 与 Caprover 或 Dokku 的比较，希望了解 Canine 的独特之处。
• [hardwaresofton] 对 Canine 的发布表示祝贺，并肯定了其产品的长足进步。
• [tonyhart7] 认为 Canine 与 Kubero 类似，但指出 Kubero 没有获得太多关注，用户可能更倾向于使用如 Coolify 这样的简单工具。
• [federicotdn] 报告了使用 Canine 创建项目时遇到的技术问题，POST 请求返回 422 错误，项目创建失败。

争议焦点：
• Canine 是否真正简化了 K8s 的使用，满足了开发者对易用性的需求。
• Canine 与类似平台（如 Kubero、Caprover、Dokku）的区别和优势。
• Canine 文档中 sarcastic 内容对用户决策的影响。
• Canine 在开发者体验和生产环境可靠性、扩展性上的表现。

data.title: Open-Source RISC-V: Energy Efficiency of Superscalar, Out-of-Order Execution
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章评估了开源RISC-V核的能效，特别是超标量乱序执行的性能。作者修改了XuanTie C910核以实现RISC-V标准的调试、中断和内存接口兼容，并提出了CVA6S+，这是一个基于CVA6核的双发射改进版，性能提升了34.4%。文章在22nm技术下对比了CVA6、CVA6S+和C910的性能、面积、功耗和能效。结果显示，CVA6S+在面积效率上领先，而C910在能量效率上具有竞争力，挑战了高性能必然伴随大面积和高能耗的传统观点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源高性能RV CPU的可行性及其相关技术问题

不同观点：
• [dkjaudyeqooe] 认为设计和实现高性能的开源RV CPU需要大量投入，单个公司可能难以承担，但如果有足够多的感兴趣的用户共同参与，就有可能实现。关键在于找到一个能够凝聚这些努力的项目。
• [Pet_Ant] 提出利用LLMs（如ChatGPT）进行语言转换的可能性，认为如果设计已经验证并理解，那么验证转换后的版本应该比从头开始容易得多，尽管这不仅仅是复制粘贴那么简单。
• [sylware] 关注当前RISC-V开源实现中的具体技术问题，特别是harts（硬件线程）是否具有存储队列和加载队列优化，如内存请求融合。这对于编写rv64汇编代码的开发者来说尤为重要。
• [fithisux] 强调RISC-V需要一个开放的生态系统来成功，包括开放的板卡和完全记录的芯片。如果CPU/GPU/DSP融合的核心能够实现，将是一个非常积极的步骤。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了具体的RISC-V开源项目，如BOOM和Xiangshan，这些项目使用Chisel语言开发，但工业电子设计自动化（EDA）工具的支持有限。
• 对LLMs在设计转换中的潜在应用进行了初步讨论，尽管具体技术细节未深入展开。
• 强调了开放硬件和文档对RISC-V生态系统成功的重要性，指出了融合CPU/GPU/DSP核心的潜在积极影响。

争议焦点：
• 目前并没有明显的争议，但不同观点反映了实现高性能开源RV CPU所面临的多方面挑战，包括技术实现、工具支持和生态系统建设。

总结：讨论围绕开源高性能RV CPU的可行性展开，涉及技术细节、工具支持和生态系统建设等多方面问题。不同参与者从各自的角度提出了见解，包括设计实现的难度、语言转换的可能性、具体技术优化问题以及开放生态系统的重要性。

Title:
Ramping Up Open-Source RISC-V Cores: Assessing the Energy Efficiency of Superscalar, Out-of-Order Execution
Authors:
Zexin Fu
,

View a PDF of the paper titled Ramping Up Open-Source RISC-V Cores: Assessing the Energy Efficiency of Superscalar, Out-of-Order Execution, by Zexin Fu and 6 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Open-source RISC-V cores are increasingly demanded in domains like automotive and space, where achieving high instructions per cycle (IPC) through superscalar and out-of-order (OoO) execution is crucial. However, high-performance open-source RISC-V cores face adoption challenges: some (e.g. BOOM, Xiangshan) are developed in Chisel with limited support from industrial electronic design automation (EDA) tools. Others, like the XuanTie C910 core, use proprietary interfaces and protocols, including non-standard AXI protocol extensions, interrupts, and debug support.
In this work, we present a modified version of the OoO C910 core to achieve full RISC-V standard compliance in its debug, interrupt, and memory interfaces. We also introduce CVA6S+, an enhanced version of the dual-issue, industry-supported open-source CVA6 core. CVA6S+ achieves 34.4% performance improvement over CVA6 core.
We conduct a detailed performance, area, power, and energy analysis on the superscalar out-of-order C910, superscalar in-order CVA6S+ and vanilla, single-issue in-order CVA6, all implemented in a 22nm technology and integrated into Cheshire, an open-source modular SoC. We examine the performance and efficiency of different microarchitectures using the same ISA, SoC, and implementation with identical technology, tools, and methodologies. The area and performance rankings of CVA6, CVA6S+, and C910 follow expected trends: compared to the scalar CVA6, CVA6S+ shows an area increase of 6% and an IPC improvement of 34.4%, while C910 exhibits a 75% increase in area and a 119.5% improvement in IPC. However, efficiency analysis reveals that CVA6S+ leads in area efficiency (GOPS/mm2), while the C910 is highly competitive in energy efficiency (GOPS/W). This challenges the common belief that high performance in superscalar and out-of-order cores inherently comes at a significant cost in area and energy efficiency.

44291204.article_summary: 这篇文章评估了开源RISC-V核的能效，特别是超标量乱序执行的性能。作者修改了XuanTie C910核以实现RISC-V标准的调试、中断和内存接口兼容，并提出了CVA6S+，这是一个基于CVA6核的双发射改进版，性能提升了34.4%。文章在22nm技术下对比了CVA6、CVA6S+和C910的性能、面积、功耗和能效。结果显示，CVA6S+在面积效率上领先，而C910在能量效率上具有竞争力，挑战了高性能必然伴随大面积和高能耗的传统观点。
44291204.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源高性能RV CPU的可行性及其相关技术问题

不同观点：
• [dkjaudyeqooe] 认为设计和实现高性能的开源RV CPU需要大量投入，单个公司可能难以承担，但如果有足够多的感兴趣的用户共同参与，就有可能实现。关键在于找到一个能够凝聚这些努力的项目。
• [Pet_Ant] 提出利用LLMs（如ChatGPT）进行语言转换的可能性，认为如果设计已经验证并理解，那么验证转换后的版本应该比从头开始容易得多，尽管这不仅仅是复制粘贴那么简单。
• [sylware] 关注当前RISC-V开源实现中的具体技术问题，特别是harts（硬件线程）是否具有存储队列和加载队列优化，如内存请求融合。这对于编写rv64汇编代码的开发者来说尤为重要。
• [fithisux] 强调RISC-V需要一个开放的生态系统来成功，包括开放的板卡和完全记录的芯片。如果CPU/GPU/DSP融合的核心能够实现，将是一个非常积极的步骤。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了具体的RISC-V开源项目，如BOOM和Xiangshan，这些项目使用Chisel语言开发，但工业电子设计自动化（EDA）工具的支持有限。
• 对LLMs在设计转换中的潜在应用进行了初步讨论，尽管具体技术细节未深入展开。
• 强调了开放硬件和文档对RISC-V生态系统成功的重要性，指出了融合CPU/GPU/DSP核心的潜在积极影响。

争议焦点：
• 目前并没有明显的争议，但不同观点反映了实现高性能开源RV CPU所面临的多方面挑战，包括技术实现、工具支持和生态系统建设。

data.title: WhatsApp introduces ads in its app
data.author: greenburger
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WhatsApp引入广告的合理性及影响

不同观点：
• **反对广告的立场**：
   - **用户体验下降**：mrtksn 认为广告会降低用户体验，并指出当前通过第三方获取利润的模式会导致注意力分散、隐私侵犯和内容操控问题。
   - **违背初衷**：robertlagrant 和 illiac786 提到WhatsApp最初承诺不会引入广告，其早期哲学是提供简单、快速、无广告的通信体验。
   - **隐私问题**：christina97 对WhatsApp声称的“端到端加密”持怀疑态度，认为这种声明有 paternalistic（家长式）的意味。
   - **对Meta的不信任**：ommz 指出Meta一贯违背最初的承诺，预计WhatsApp最终会充斥广告和“间谍软件”。

• **支持付费模式**：
   - **回归付费使用**：mrtksn 提议回归到用户付费使用的模式，认为这样可以避免通过第三方获取利润所带来的各种问题。
   - **愿意付费**：perks_12 表示在德国，WhatsApp具有很高的地位，自己愿意为使用API付费，以避免广告和糟糕的用户体验。
   - **历史经验**：charles_f 提到WhatsApp在被收购前是付费的，并且自己很乐意付费以避免广告。

• **广告不可避免的观点**：
   - **市场需求**：kunzhi 认为大多数用户希望应用保持免费，即使这意味着要忍受广告，因为他们更关心获得“免费”的服务。
   - **历史规律**：ommz 指出Meta/Facebook一贯会在其收购的平台上引入广告，这是不可避免的。

补充讨论：
• **技术手段规避广告**：vachina 提到如果广告不能通过DNS等方式屏蔽，将转向使用Signal等其他应用。
• **时间问题**：snapcaster 对广告引入的时间感到惊讶，但认为这是迟早会发生的事情。
• **法律和网络效应**：leokennis 提到在荷兰，WhatsApp即使引入广告也能因网络效应而继续保持用户基础，因为用户别无选择。

争议焦点：
• **广告引入与用户隐私及体验的冲突**：一方认为广告会严重影响用户体验和隐私，另一方认为这是保持服务免费的必要手段。
• **Meta是否会坚守承诺**：对Meta是否会真正遵守其在隐私和广告方面的承诺持怀疑态度。

总结：讨论主要围绕WhatsApp引入广告的合理性、对用户体验和隐私的影响以及是否回归付费模式展开，反映了用户对广告和隐私问题的强烈关注。

data.title: Transparent peer review to be extended to all of Nature's research papers
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 自2020年以来，《Nature》期刊允许作者选择将同行评审文件与论文一同发表。从2025年6月16日起，所有新提交并发表为研究文章的手稿将自动包含评审报告和作者回应的链接，评审者身份保持匿名，除非他们选择公开。此举旨在增加科学过程的透明度，揭示论文形成的细节，增强公众对科学的信任。通过公开评审报告，可以让更多人了解科学讨论的过程，特别是对早期研究人员有重要价值。科学知识随着新证据的出现而演变，而同行评审是提升论文质量的关键部分，应该被视为科学记录的重要组成部分。此举也是对科研评价方式变革的响应。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：透明同行评审制度及其对科学界的影响

不同观点：
• probably_wrong：认为透明评审可能对科学不利。理由包括对拥有大社交媒体影响力的研究人员的拒绝可能引发攻击，以及女性和有评审经验的研究人员对公共评审的支持度较低，这可能导致该制度仅有利于已经处于学术圈内的人。引用了一个2019年ACL的调查来支持其观点。

• aDyslecticCrow：支持透明同行评审，认为它可以提高学术信任度，并应对公众对科学信任度下降的问题。特别提到AI可能进一步降低科学质量，因此更严格的出版流程是必要的。

• jostmey：认为透明评审只解决了同行评审问题的一小部分，真正的挑战在于评审者无法复制研究，导致他们只能寻找论文中的不一致之处，可能忽略反常数据，且数据造假也可能未被质疑。

• eig：支持透明评审，认为它对个人论文发表过程有帮助，并希望这能减少大实验室通过关系更容易在高影响力期刊发表文章的情况。

• WhatsTheBigIdea：对透明评审持谨慎支持态度，但认为科学的本质是质疑和怀疑，而不是简单地“信任科学”。强调科学应接受来自各方面的质疑，透明评审可能是朝正确方向迈出的一步，但不能解决所有信任问题。

• trelane：指出透明评审揭示的争议可能只是更大问题的表面现象，暗示该制度可能揭示更深层次的学术问题。

• dr_dshiv：主张建立更多科学团体，回顾历史上科学评审是基于高标准和学术共同体，而非现代的所谓“客观性”，认为科学是“友谊”。

• lenerdenator：对透明评审的概念表示困惑，质疑为何这种做法不是早已普遍存在，暗示对学术界的现有实践缺乏了解。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于透明同行评审是否能真正提高科学质量和公众信任，以及该制度是否会带来新的问题，如对评审者的攻击和学术不公。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是科学的本质和公众对科学的信任问题，透明评审是否能重新赢得公众信任，还是仅为表面措施。
• 不同的学术背景（如本科研究助理与有经验的研究人员）对透明评审的看法和理解存在差异。

A published research paper is the result of an extensive conversation between authors and reviewers, guided by editors.
Credit: Getty
Since 2020,
Nature
has offered authors the opportunity to have their
peer-review file published alongside their paper
. Our colleagues at
Nature Communications
have been doing so since 2016
. Until now,
Nature
authors could opt in to this process of transparent peer review. From 16 June, however, new submissions of manuscripts that are published as research articles in
Nature
will automatically include a link to the reviewers’ reports and author responses.
It means that, over time, more
Nature
papers will include a peer-review file. The identity of the reviewers will remain anonymous, unless they choose otherwise — as happens now. But the exchanges between the referees and the authors will be accessible to all. Our aim in doing so is to open up what many see as the ‘black box’ of science, shedding light on how a research paper is made. This serves to increase transparency and (we hope) to build trust in the scientific process.
Research evaluation needs to change with the times
As
we have written previously
, a published research paper is the result of an extensive conversation between authors and reviewers, guided by editors. These discussions, which can last for months, aim to improve a study’s clarity and the robustness of its conclusions. It is a hugely important process that should receive increased recognition, including acknowledgement of the reviewers involved, if they choose to be named. For early-career researchers, there is great value in seeing inside a process that is key to their career development. Making peer-reviewer reports public also enriches science communication: it’s a chance to add to the ‘story’ of how a result is arrived at, or a conclusion supported, even if it includes only the perspectives of authors and reviewers. The full story of a paper is, of course, more complex, involving many other contributors.
Many people think of science as something fixed and unchanging. But scientific knowledge evolves as new or more-nuanced evidence comes to light. Scientists constantly discuss their results, yet these debates are not contained in research papers and often remain unreported in wider science-communication efforts.
Three-year trial shows support for recognizing peer reviewers
The COVID-19 pandemic provided a brief interlude during which much of the world got to see how research works,
almost in real time
. It’s easy to forget that, right from the start, we were continuously learning something new about the nature and behaviour of the SARS-CoV-2 virus. On television screens, in newspapers and on social media worldwide, scientists were discussing among themselves and with public audiences the nature of the virus, how it infects people and how it spreads. They were debating treatments and prevention methods, constantly adjusting everyone’s knowledge
as fresh evidence came to light
. And then, it went mostly back to business as usual.
We hope that publishing the peer-reviewer reports of all newly submitted
Nature
papers shows, in a small way, that this doesn’t need to remain the case.
Nature
started mandating peer review for all published research articles only in 1973 (
M. Baldwin
Notes Rec.
69
, 337–352; 2015
). But the convention in most fields is still to keep the content of these peer-review exchanges confidential. That has meant that the wider research community, and the world, has had few opportunities to learn what is discussed.
Peer review improves papers. The exchanges between authors and referees should be seen as a crucial part of the scientific record, just as they are a key part of doing and disseminating research.

data.title: Scientists genetically engineer a lethal mosquito STD to combat malaria
data.author: burnt-resistor
data.article_summary: 科学家通过基因工程改造了一种致命真菌（Metarhizium），以对抗疟疾等蚊媒疾病。这种真菌通过传播性毒素杀死按蚊（传播疟疾的蚊子）的雌蚊，而雄蚊在交配时传播这种真菌孢子，形成类似性传播疾病的效果。实验显示，感染这种改造真菌的雌蚊死亡率高达90%。该方法利用蚊子的自然交配行为，且对人类无害。由于蚊子对传统杀虫剂和药物逐渐产生抗药性，这种生物控制方法提供了一种新的有效手段来抑制蚊子种群并减少疾病传播。研究已发表于《科学报告》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过生物技术或化学手段控制蚊子种群以应对蚊媒疾病的可行性与潜在风险

不同观点：
• **支持生物技术控制蚊子**：有人提到在加州原本计划推出相关措施但被环保组织阻止，同时个人在洛杉矶使用"蚊子 Dunk"（生物控制方法）取得了一些成功，但认为需要邻居配合才能更有效（[rcpt]）。此外，还有人引用科学文章，指出一种对人类无害但能杀死蚊子的转基因真菌，认为这种方法类似于不断演化的治疗手段，类似于噬菌体疗法（[chasil]）。

• **质疑生物技术干预**：有人对消灭食物链底端的物种（如蚊子）表示担忧，并以讽刺语气质疑这种做法可能带来的生态风险，例如是否需要青蛙和燕子等捕食者（[peterlada]）。其他用户则以讽刺方式表达对基因工程干预可能带来的不可预见后果的担忧，提到如"冬天时大猩猩会冻死"等极端假设场景（[recursivedoubts]），以及简单地问"什么可能出错？"来质疑这类技术的潜在风险（[DrNosferatu], [mont_tag]）。

补充讨论：
• **专家参与**：一位曾经在相关领域工作过的用户提到自己曾在Raymond St. Leger的实验室工作，并愿意传递讨论中的问题，显示出讨论中可能有专业知识的参与（[pazimzadeh]）。

争议焦点：
• **生物技术干预的风险与收益**：一方认为生物技术如转基因真菌是控制蚊媒疾病的有希望手段，另一方则担心消灭蚊子等物种可能带来的生态连锁反应和不可预见的后果。

Jay Kakade

Scientists genetically engineer a lethal mosquito STD to combat malaria
Mosquitoes spread dangerous diseases like dengue and malaria to hundreds of millions of people each year
Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
View 1 Image
1
/
1
Mosquitoes spread dangerous diseases like dengue and malaria to hundreds of millions of people each year
Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
Mosquitoes have long been among humanity’s most formidable adversaries, plaguing us for thousands of years and causing more deaths than any other animal. With traditional control methods facing mounting resistance, researchers are seeking innovative ways to combat mosquito-borne disease.
Now, entomologists at the University of Maryland have bioengineered a deadly fungus that spreads sexually in
Anopheles
(malaria-spreading) mosquitoes. The naturally occurring fungus called
Metarhizium
produces insect-specific neurotoxins, potent enough to kill female mosquitoes – the ones that spread disease. By dusting male mosquitoes with modified fungal spores, the team essentially created a sexually transmitted infection for mosquitoes.
For reference, this is not the first time that scientists have exploited mosquito mating habits to curb populations. Recently, researchers modified
male mosquitoes to secrete toxic proteins in their semen
, to kill female mosquitoes after mating.
While
Metarhizium
was already known to transmit through sex, natural strains resulted in very low mortality. In field trials conducted in Burkina Faso, West Africa, the newly engineered version proved far more lethal; nearly 90% of females died within two weeks of mating with infected males, compared to just a 4% mortality rate with wild-type
Metarhizium
. Notably, the fungal infection did not deter female mosquitoes from mating with infected males.
Despite being lethal to mosquitoes, the transgenic
Metarhizium
fungus is harmless in humans. Once exposed, male mosquitoes with the fungal strain can transmit spores for up to 24 hours to multiple mating partners, making the method ideal to deploy in the environment.
“What makes this fungus particularly promising is that it works with existing mosquito behavior rather than against their natural habits," says study co-author Raymond St. Leger. "Unlike pesticides or other chemical control methods that mosquitoes can develop resistance to, this method uses the mosquitoes’ own biology to deliver the control agent."
But why are such approaches necessary?
Primarily, it's due to the mosquito’s remarkable adaptability. Recently, mosquitoes and mosquito-borne parasites have developed resistance to chemical treatments and antimalarial drugs. Some mosquito populations have even adapted by avoiding bed nets and repellents, choosing instead to rest outdoors.
“It’s essentially an arms race between the mosquitoes and us," says St. Leger. "Just as they keep adapting to what we create, we have to continuously develop new and creative ways to fight them,”
The study was published in
Scientific Reports
.

University of Maryland

44291963.article_summary: 科学家通过基因工程改造了一种致命真菌（Metarhizium），以对抗疟疾等蚊媒疾病。这种真菌通过传播性毒素杀死按蚊（传播疟疾的蚊子）的雌蚊，而雄蚊在交配时传播这种真菌孢子，形成类似性传播疾病的效果。实验显示，感染这种改造真菌的雌蚊死亡率高达90%。该方法利用蚊子的自然交配行为，且对人类无害。由于蚊子对传统杀虫剂和药物逐渐产生抗药性，这种生物控制方法提供了一种新的有效手段来抑制蚊子种群并减少疾病传播。研究已发表于《科学报告》。

data.title: Dull Men’s Club
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary:
《沉闷男俱乐部：以沉闷为荣》一文介绍了这个以分享日常生活枯燥乏味之事为主题的国际线上俱乐部。俱乐部拥有数百万成员，他们自豪地展示自己的沉闷，庆祝平凡琐事，以讽刺和自嘲的幽默为特色。俱乐部的规则严格，杜绝任何“过于 exciting”的内容，如bitmoji头像和感叹号。创始人Grover Click表示，俱乐部旨在提供一个安全、礼貌的空间，讨论日常琐事，禁止政治、宗教和粗俗内容。

沉闷男俱乐部起源于1980年代的纽约，最初是一个玩笑，如今已发展成拥有190万成员的Facebook群组，并衍生了年度奖项、出版物和周边商品。澳大利亚分支有8000名成员，竞争性的“比谁更沉闷”成为一种乐趣。成员Andrew McKean在搬入护理设施后，通过俱乐部找到了志同道合的朋友，将沉闷的日常变得诗意而感人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“ dull”（无趣）的概念以及与之相关的各种社群、俱乐部和内容的讨论。

不同观点：
• **rester324**：认为无趣是一种视角问题。自己虽然看似无趣，但孩子和家人却很喜欢他的陪伴，表明“无趣”是相对的。他通过接受自己的“无趣”，不再在意外界的看法。
• **ecshafer**：提到Facebook上的Dull Men's Club，实际上分享的是一些日常生活中的小趣事，而不是真正的“无趣”，更像是一种古怪的幽默。

• **mafro**：表示Dull Men's Club具有英国式的自嘲幽默，参与者都乐于分享和接受彼此的“无趣”。

After moving to a care facility, Andrew McKean found his tribe – men who share his ironic, self-deprecating view of the world.
Photograph: Bec Lorrimer/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
After moving to a care facility, Andrew McKean found his tribe – men who share his ironic, self-deprecating view of the world.
Photograph: Bec Lorrimer/The Guardian
Health & wellbeing
Meet the members of the Dull Men’s Club: ‘Some of them would bore the ears off you’
An international club where dull people meet online to share the tedium of everyday lives is immensely popular. But for one man it’s a place of poignant connection
Get Guardian Australia’s weekend culture and lifestyle email
Susan Chenery
Sun 8 Jun 2025 11.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 9 Jun 2025 01.41 EDT
Share
T
he 18th-century English writer Samuel Johnson once wrote, “He is not only dull himself; he is the cause of dullness in others’. It’s a sentiment eagerly embraced by The Dull Men’s Club. Several million members in a number of connected Facebook groups strive to cause dullness in others on a daily basis. In this club, they wear their dullness with pride. The duller the better. This is where the nerds of the world unite.
“Posts that contain bitmoji-avatar-things are far too exciting, and will probably get deleted,” warn the rules of the Dull Men’s Club (Australian branch).
Maintaining standards of dullness is paramount. Alan Goodwin in the UK recently worried that seeing a lesser spotted woodpecker in his garden might be “a bit too exciting” for the group. In the same week, a flight tracker struggled to keep his excitement to an acceptable level when military jets suddenly appeared on his screen.
View image in fullscreen
Andrew McKean moved to a care facility after a heart attack.
Photograph: Bec Lorrimer/The Guardian
This is the place for quirky hobbies, obscure interests, the examination of small, ordinary things. It is a place to celebrate the mundane, the quotidian. It is a gentle antidote to pouting influencers and the often toxic internet; a bastion of civility; a polite clarion call to reclaim the ordinary. Above all, it is whimsical, deeply ironic, self-effacing and sarcastic humour.
There is an art to being both dull and droll. “It’s tongue-in-cheek humour,” says founder Grover Click (a pseudonym chosen for its dullness). “A safe place to comment on daily things.” Exclamation marks, he says, “are far too exciting.” (On his site, ridicule is against the rules, as is politics, religion, and swearing.)
There is, says Bt Humble, a moderator for the Australian branch, “a level of one-upmanship. It’s sort of competitive dullness.” Dull people trying to out-dull each other.
View image in fullscreen
In his writing, McKean has elevated the dull institutional days into something poetic and poignant.
Photograph: Bec Lorrimer/The Guardian
Are there people who are just too exciting for the club? “There isn’t actually a mandatory level of dullness,” he admits, although some of the members he has met “would bore the ears off you”.
It all started in New York in the early 1980s. Click, now 85, and his friends were sitting at the long bar of the New York Athletic club reading magazine articles about boxing, fencing, judo and wrestling. “One of my mates said, ‘Dude, we don’t do any of those things.’” They had to face it. They were dull. They decided to embrace their dullness.
As a joke, they started The Dull Men’s Club, which involved some very silly, dull activities. They chartered a tour bus but didn’t go anywhere. “We toured the bus. We walked around the outside of the bus a few times. And the driver explained the tyre pressures and turned on the windscreen wipers.”
In 1996, when Click moved to the UK, his nephew offered to build a website for “that silly Dull Men’s Club”.
Sign up for the fun stuff with our rundown of must-reads, pop culture and tips for the weekend, every Saturday morning
Today, Click’s copyrighted Dull Men’s Club Facebook group has 1.9 million members. There is an annual calendar featuring people with peculiar hobbies, a book – Dull Men of Great Britain – merchandise and not one but two awards: Anorak of the Year in the UK and DMC Person of the Year for the rest of the world. There are also numerous copycat Dull Men’s Clubs, including one that has 1.7 million members. Click is “very surprised” that so many people identify as dull. The Australian club has 8,000 members. Comparatively small but definitely holding its own in the dullness department.
View image in fullscreen
Andrew self-publishes books and regularly posts his writing on Facebook group, including the Dull Men’s Club.
Photograph: Bec Lorrimer/The Guardian
Much of the minutiae of life gets on members’ nerves, as does poor workmanship. Five hundred amused comments followed a post about coat hangers inserted into hoops on rails in hotel rooms. “That would keep me up all night,” said one person.

data.title: Object personification in autism: This paper will be sad if you don't read (2018)
data.author: oliverkwebb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了自闭症个体中将人类特征赋予非人类物体的现象，即物体拟人化。通过在线调查，研究比较了87位自闭症成人和263位非自闭症成人的拟人化倾向。结果显示，自闭症个体更常经历物体拟人化，且这种现象可能在自闭症群体中持续更久。尽管许多自闭症患者感到这种体验令他们困扰，但研究强调了理解这一现象的重要性，并建议提供支持结构。这与自闭症患者的情感识别困难形成对比，提出了对拟人化现象的新理解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人对非人类物体赋予人性特征（人格化）的现象，特别是在自闭症群体中的表现，以及不同个体在感受和处理这种现象上的差异。

不同观点：
• [sctb] 认为自己作为自闭症个体，虽然没有将人性特征赋予物体，但会对损坏或失去功能的物体产生情感反应，比如一把钝的刀或凌乱的房间会引发一种“悲伤”或“缺乏尊重”的感觉。这种情感反应会延伸到无生命的物体上。

• [neilv] 提出是否有些人对“系统”有情感反应，比如在设计或管理复杂系统时，会对系统的各个部分产生情感上的关注或喜好。他认为这种能力在人群中的分布并不均匀。

• [qoez] 认为非自闭症的“正常”人更倾向于将非人类物体人格化，并提出有些人会被大语言模型的输出欺骗，认为其有真实的人类情感，而这可能与这种人格化倾向有关。他作为自闭症个体，从未觉得LLM是真实的人类。

• 争议的焦点在于自闭症个体是否比非自闭症个体更倾向于对物体进行人格化，以及相关研究的可靠性和样本量问题。

• 讨论中还涉及对系统和复杂物品的情感反应，扩展了物体人格化现象的范围。

Abstract
Object personification is the attribution of human characteristics to non-human agents. In online forums, autistic individuals commonly report experiencing this phenomenon. Given that approximately half of all autistic individuals experience difficulties identifying their own emotions, the suggestion that object personification may be a feature of autism seems almost paradoxical. Why would a person experience sympathy for objects, when they struggle to understand and verbalise the emotions of other people as well as their own? An online survey was used to assess tendency for personification in 87 autistic and 263 non-autistic adults. Together, our results indicate that object personification occurs commonly among autistic individuals, and perhaps more often (and later in life) than in the general population. Given that in many cases, autistic people report their personification experiences as distressing, it is important to consider the reasons for the increased personification and identify structures for support.
Keywords:
anthropomorphism; autism spectrum disorders; cognition (attention, learning, memory); perception; personification.

data.title: Why today's graduates are screwed
data.author: petethomas
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了当前大学毕业生面临的严峻就业市场问题。过去几十年，通过上大学、找一份研究生工作从而过上美好生活的路径很明确，但如今，勤奋的年轻人选择更少，机会更有限。文章还提到其他经济话题，如中国能否重夺IPO桂冠、香港与大陆的市场对比、以色利与伊朗战争对油价的影响、如何投资巨额遗产、乌克兰无人机成功的经济教训、以及欧洲股市和美国工业幻想的困境等。文章反映出全球经济不确定性对年轻人和市场的多重影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章观点的评价与讨论，特别是关于科技技能普及、年轻人就业市场以及大学学历的价值等问题。

不同观点：
• [tracerbulletx] 认为文章质量较低，指出文章存在许多错误和显而易见的模糊观点，尤其是关于智能手机让科技技能更普及的说法没有逻辑性。
• [pixelpoet] 支持 [tracerbulletx] 的观点，通过个人经历（自学编程）说明现代智能手机并未教授用户编程或操作系统基础知识，认为文章作者缺乏对计算机的理解。他还引用了一篇2021年的文章来支持自己的观点，并质疑谷歌或苹果是否有意识地选择强化被动消费。
• [ahartmetz] 则关注就业市场，指出每次经济低迷时，某些群体受影响最严重，并提到关于年轻人就业问题的文章经常出现。
• [pedalpete] 提出另一个角度，讨论了就业市场中的供需矛盾：一方面抱怨好工作不多，另一方面又认为随着年长者退休，没有足够的人来填补空缺岗位。他还提到年龄歧视和雇佣高级人才的高成本问题，并分享了自己在创业公司中帮助毕业生过渡到职场的经验。

补充讨论：
• [darepublic] 使用网络语言调侃当前年轻人的困境，提到"cooked"（意为糟糕、完蛋了）这个新世代用语。
• [pixelpoet] 对文章中提到的“欧盟15至24岁年轻人从事金融业”表示怀疑，特别是针对德国的情况，质疑这些年轻人是否在非法工作，并期待更多信息。
• [pedalpete] 进一步讨论了大学学历的必要性，认为文章未提及学历是否是进入职场的必要条件，并分享了自己没有学位但在职场上未遇到太多障碍的经历。

争议焦点：
• 文章关于智能手机让科技技能更普及的观点遭到多位评论者质疑，他们认为智能手机并未教授用户编程或操作系统基础知识。
• 年轻人就业市场的实际情况和文章描述可能存在差距，特别是关于金融业就业的描述引发质疑。
• 大学学历在进入职场时的必要性也被多位评论者提及，并提出不同看法。

总结：评论者们主要对文章中关于科技技能普及和年轻人就业市场的观点提出质疑，并通过个人经历和外部资料支持自己的论点。同时，大学学历的价值和就业市场的供需矛盾也是讨论的重点。

data.title: Meta ignores RFC 2920; ZuckMail can't send mail to servers running OpenSMTPD
data.author: pghatedphones
data.article_summary: OpenBSD用户Mikolaj Kucharski报告其运行OpenSMTPd的SMTP服务器无法接收来自WhatsApp的验证码邮件。日志显示错误信息："smtp bad-input result=500 5.5.1 Invalid command: Pipelining not supported"。Omar Polo回复称这是因为OpenSMTPd不支持Pipelining，而这是已知问题，责任在于Meta的邮件服务器。Omar认为缺乏Pipelining支持并非坏事，可能不算严重的缺陷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：邮件传输中的问题及其可能的原因

不同观点：
• [tedunangst] 认为不支持流水线（pipelining）是一个有效且低 effort 的垃圾邮件过滤方法。他的论据是，垃圾邮件发送者没有时间等待响应代码，他们只负责发送信息并迅速转移到下一个目标。

• [AnotherGoodName] 认为问题可能更广泛，不仅仅与 OpenSMTPD 有关。他提到自己也遇到了 Gmail 无法接收邮件的问题，并推测 Meta 可能存在邮件服务器全面故障的问题。他还指出，OpenSMTPD 的回复将问题归咎于 Meta，并认为这种归因是正确的。

• [eqvinox] 补充说，exim 如果配置得当（例如合理的初始垃圾邮件屏障），也会因为这种行为拒绝邮件。他提到这种行为在垃圾邮件中很常见，以至于他从日志中过滤掉了这些信息以避免垃圾信息堆积。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于问题的根源。有些人认为问题出在 OpenSMTPD，而 [AnotherGoodName] 则认为问题可能出在 Meta 的邮件服务器上，这表明问题的影响范围可能更广。

• 各个评论者都提供了技术细节支持他们的观点，例如流水线支持的缺失、邮件服务器日志的处理等，显示出对邮件传输协议和配置有深入了解。

• 讨论中还提到了不同邮件传输代理（MTA）如 OpenSMTPD 和 exim 的行为差异，这可能表明问题的复杂性和多样性。

data.title: Tiny-diffusion: A minimal implementation of probabilistic diffusion models
data.author: BraverHeart
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为 **tiny-diffusion** 的最小PyTorch实现，用于2D数据集的概率扩散模型。项目包括前向扩散过程（逐渐破坏数据）和反向过程（恢复数据分布）的可视化。作者进行了多项消融实验，研究了学习率、模型大小、时间步数、方差调度等对模型表现的影响。结果显示，学习率对模型训练至关重要，而模型容量（隐藏层大小和数量）并非瓶颈。此外，时间步和输入的位置嵌入对模型有帮助，但具体方法不关键。项目参考了多个现有扩散模型实现和数据集，如Datasaurus Dozen。用户可通过运行 `python ddpm.py -h` 来探索训练选项。

tiny-diffusion
A minimal PyTorch implementation of probabilistic diffusion models for 2D datasets. Get started by running
python ddpm.py -h
to explore the available options for training.
Forward process
A visualization of the forward diffusion process being applied to a dataset of one thousand 2D points. Note that the dinosaur is not a single training example, it represents each 2D point in the dataset.
Reverse process
This illustration shows how the reverse process recovers the distribution of the training data.
Ablations
I have run a series of ablations experiments on hyperparameters, such as learning rate and model size, and visualized the learning process. The columns in the graphs represent the checkpoint epoch, and the rows indicate the hyperparameter values. Each cell displays one thousand generated 2D points.
learning rate
The learning process is sensitive to the learning rate. At first, the model's output was poor, causing me to suspect a bug. However, simply changing the learning rate value resolved the problem.
dataset
The current model configuration doesn't work well on the
line
dataset, which I consider the most basic among them. The corners should be clear and sharp, but they are fuzzy.
num timesteps
A longer diffusion process results in a better output. With fewer timesteps, the dinosaur is incomplete, missing points from the top and bottom.
variance schedule
The quadratic schedule does not yield better results. Other schedules like cosine or sigmoid should also be considered.
hidden size
The capacity of the model doesn't seem to be a bottleneck, as similar results are obtained across various hidden layer sizes.
number of hidden layers
As in the hidden size ablation run, the capacity of the model does not seem to be a limiting factor.
positional embedding (timestep)
The model benefits from the timestep information, but the specific method of encoding the timestep is not important.
positional embedding (inputs)
The use of sinusoidal embeddings for the inputs helps with learning high-frequency functions in low-dimensional problem domains, such as mapping each (x, y) pixel coordinate to (r, g, b) color, as demonstrated in
this study
. The same holds true in the current scenario.

data.title: Stop Writing Brittle Playwright Tests: Why YAML-Based Testing Is the Future
data.author: suchuanyi
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了从传统Playwright测试转向基于YAML测试的优势，后者通过简化测试编写和提高可维护性，使团队中每个人都能参与自动化测试。传统Playwright测试存在代码冗长、硬编码值、复用性差、技术门槛高等问题，而YAML测试使用清晰的自然语言描述步骤，易于理解和修改，并支持环境变量和可重用组件。YAML测试还具备智能标签过滤和自动生成报告功能，显著减少了环境变化引起的测试失败。实施YAML测试后，团队新成员上手时间从3天缩短至30分钟，且整个团队都能编写和修改测试。这种方法提高了开发效率，简化了QA和DevOps工作流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用大型语言模型（LLM）和工具（如Playwright、Claude Code等）进行测试的有效性和可行性讨论

不同观点：
• [moomin] 认为使用LLM重新发明Cucumber（一种BDD测试工具）可能效果更差。虽然Playwright测试可行，但需要注重设计，否则可能导致混乱。使用steps文件是一种方式，但保持代码结构的规范性同样重要。不能指望堆砌1000行脚本代码而忽视代码结构的基本原则。

• [ohdeargodno] 强烈反对用基于LLM的测试替代不可靠的UI测试，认为这会带来更多问题，例如测试失败后需要花费大量时间调整提示。现有的测试工具问题很多（如仅适用于浏览器、不可重复、隐藏验证等）。他们强调，主要的UI测试工具应该是可访问性测试，如果无法通过可访问性元素进行测试，说明产品本身可访问性不足。同时提到Maestro工具在表达性和脚本开放性上找到了一种平衡。

• 可访问性测试被[ohdeargodno]视为比UI测试更基础和重要的工具，强调了产品可访问性在测试中的优先地位。

Stop Writing Brittle Playwright Tests: Why YAML-Based Testing is the Future
四眼蒙面侠
Follow
6 min read
·
1 day ago
--
Listen
Share
How a simple YAML configuration built for Claude Code and Playwright MCP transformed our testing workflow and made automation accessible to everyone on the team
If you’ve ever maintained a large Playwright test suite, you know the pain. Hundreds of lines of JavaScript scattered across dozens of files. Hardcoded values that break when environments change. Test logic so complex that only the original author dares to modify it.
What if I told you there’s a better way? A way to write tests that are readable by anyone, maintainable by design, and powerful enough to handle complex workflows?
Enter YAML-based Playwright testing for Claude Code — a paradigm shift that’s changing how teams approach test automation by leveraging the power of Claude Code’s AI capabilities and Playwright MCP’s browser automation.
The Problem with Traditional Playwright Tests
Let’s be honest about traditional Playwright tests:
// Traditional Playwright test - 50+ lines of code
test('complete order flow', async ({ page }) => {
await page.goto('https://example.com');
await page.fill('[data-testid="username"]', 'user123');
await page.fill('[data-testid="password"]', 'pass456');
await page.click('[data-testid="login-btn"]');
await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Dashboard');
// ... 40+ more lines of clicking, filling, asserting
// ... hardcoded values everywhere
// ... no reusability between tests
});
Problems:
❌ Verbose and complex — Simple actions buried in boilerplate
❌ Hardcoded values — Environment changes break everything
❌ Poor reusability — Copy-paste leads to maintenance nightmares
❌ Technical barrier — Only developers can write/modify tests
❌ Scattered logic — Related tests live in different files
The YAML Revolution: Tests That Make Sense
Now imagine the same test written in YAML:
# test-cases/order.yml
tags:
- smoke
- order
- checkout
steps:
- include: "login"
- "Click Add to Cart button for first product"
- "Click Add to Cart button for second product"
- "Click shopping cart icon in top right"
- "Enter First Name"
- "Enter Last Name"
- "Enter Postal Code"
- "Click Continue button"
- "Click Finish button"
- "Verify page displays Thank you for your order!"
- include: "cleanup"
Immediate benefits:
✅ Crystal clear intent — Anyone can understand what this test does
✅ Natural language — Steps read like user stories
✅ Reusable components — Login and cleanup are shared across tests
✅ Environment agnostic — No hardcoded values in sight
The Magic Behind the Simplicity
1. Reusable Step Libraries
Common workflows become building blocks:
# steps/login.yml
steps:
- "Open {{BASE_URL}} page"
- "Fill username field with {{TEST_USERNAME}}"
- "Fill password field with {{TEST_PASSWORD}}"
- "Click login button"
- "Verify page displays Swag Labs"
Write once, use everywhere. No more copy-paste madness.
2. Environment Variable Magic
Different environments? No problem:
# .env.dev
BASE_URL=https://dev.example.com
TEST_USERNAME=dev_user
# .env.prod
BASE_URL=https://example.com
TEST_USERNAME=prod_user
Same tests, different environments. Automatically.
3. Intelligent Tag Filtering
Run exactly what you need:
# Run only smoke tests
/run-yaml-test tags:smoke
# Run order AND checkout tests
/run-yaml-test tags:order,checkout
# Run smoke OR critical tests
/run-yaml-test tags:smoke|critical
No more running the entire suite when you only changed the login flow.
4. Smart Reporting
Automatically generated HTML reports with:
✅ Step-by-step execution details
✅ Environment configuration
✅ Screenshots and artifacts
✅ Success/failure statistics
Real-World Impact: A Case Study
Before YAML testing:
📊 2,000+ lines of Playwright JavaScript
⏱️ 3 days to onboard new QA team members
🐛 15+ test failures per environment change
👥 Only 3 developers could modify tests
After YAML testing:
📊 200 lines of readable YAML
⏱️ 30 minutes to onboard new team members
🐛 0 test failures during environment changes
👥 Entire team can write and modify tests
Why This Matters for Your Team
For Developers:
Less time writing boilerplate, more time building features
Tests that actually document your application’s behavior
No more “let me just quickly fix this test” rabbit holes
For QA Engineers:
Focus on test strategy, not JavaScript syntax
Rapid test creation and modification
Clear visibility into test coverage
For Product Managers:
Tests that read like acceptance criteria
Easy to verify that tests match requirements
Confidence that important flows are covered
For DevOps:
Predictable test execution across environments
Clear failure reporting and debugging
Easy integration with CI/CD pipelines
Technical Architecture: How It Works
This YAML Playwright testing framework is specifically designed for Claude Code and Playwright MCP. The framework consists of several key components:
Claude Code Integration
AI-Powered Execution: Claude Code’s AI interprets natural language t

这篇文章总结了软件复杂性的三种不同概念：

1. **Rich Hickey的复杂性概念**：Hickey认为简单性意味着单一性，不涉及其他事物（如状态、对象等）。他强调“简”与“易”的区别，简单是客观的，而容易则是主观的。复杂性会削弱理解，导致难以调试和修改。他主张通过消除“交织”（complect）来实现简单性，例如通过值而非变量管理状态。

2. **John Ousterhout的复杂性概念**：Ousterhout认为复杂性使系统难以理解和修改。他强调代码的“显而易见性”，即开发者能迅速理解代码并做出正确修改。复杂性源于依赖性和模糊性，依赖性指代码间的关联性，模糊性则指认知负荷和未知因素。他主张通过减少依赖和模糊来降低复杂性。

3. **Zach Tellman的复杂性概念**：Tellman关注复杂性如何影响系统的设计和理解。他强调分解复杂性，使每个部分独立易懂，并通过设计模式和良好实践来实现这一点。

这三种概念共同强调了理解和修改软件系统时减少复杂性的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件复杂性与简单性的定义和衡量标准

不同观点：
• **Tellman的观点**：简单性不是软件的内在属性，而是软件与我们期望之间的契合。这种定义强调了主观性，认为简单性取决于人类对软件系统的心里模型能否准确预测软件行为。这种观点将重点放在人类对软件的理解和操作能力上。

• **Hickey的观点**：简单性是客观的，可以通过关注点（concerns）或“折叠”的数量来衡量。然而，这种观点的争议在于如何界定这些关注点，因为不同人的风格和系统知识会导致不同的结果，使得“客观性”难以成立。

• **Ousterhout的观点**：被认为是最具体的，相比之下其他两种观点更为主观。Ousterhout强调依赖性的问题，区分了代码库或共享代码的依赖与系统各部分假设的依赖。

• **burakemir的观点**：在实际操作中，例如处理分布式系统问题时，客观的改进可能比考虑期望更为重要。这种观点强调在特定情境下，客观性对解决问题和防止未来失败的重要性。

• **0xbadcafebee的观点**：将软件讨论分为哲学、科学和功能三个层面。哲学层面涉及人类对软件本质的理解和解释，科学层面涉及计算机科学的客观性，而功能层面则是日常的软件开发实践。这种观点认为大多数开发者关注的是功能层面，而非哲学或科学层面。

• **adityaathalye的观点**：将软件复杂性类比为火箭方程，认为复杂性是一个动态的多维度现象，行为是关键因素。这种观点强调复杂性在时间和空间上的变化，并用生物学、人工智能、物理学和数学的多学科背景来支持其观点。

补充讨论：
• **amelius的观点**：提出正交性（orthogonality）在软件复杂性讨论中的重要性，尽管原文未提及。

• **readthenotes1的观点**：引用了研究文章，指出大多数复杂性度量与代码行数（LOC）高度相关，认为即使不使用复杂的度量方法，仅通过LOC也能大致评估复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 简单性是主观还是客观的：Tellman和Hickey的观点在此问题上存在明显对立，前者强调主观性，后者试图以客观标准衡量。

• 复杂性的衡量标准：不同观点提出了不同的衡量标准，如心理模型预测能力、关注点数量、依赖性、代码行数等。

• 哲学与科学层面的讨论价值：0xbadcafebee认为哲学讨论虽然重要但不如科学和功能层面的实际操作直接，而其他观点则认为哲学层面的讨论对理解软件本质有帮助。

A meta-analysis of three different notions of software complexity
I want to discuss three different notions of software complexity:
Rich Hickey’s notion of complexity, as explained in his talk
Simple Made Easy
.
John Ousterhout’s notion of complexity, as explained in his book
A Philosophy of Software Design
.
Zach Tellman’s notion of complexity, as explained in his newsletter
Explaining Software Design
.
I’ve picked these three because I’ve found them to be at least somewhat coherent,
and the former two to be (relatively) well-known;
this blog post is not meant to be exhaustive
of all different definitions of complexity that have been
offered over the years.
The definitions summarized
(Formatting note: exact quotes are taken from the above-mentioned work.)
Hickey complexity
Hickey defines something as being simple as having some kind of oneness - he uses the phrases “one fold/braid, one role, one task, one concept, one dimension.” Hickey states, “When you’re looking for something simple, you want to see it have focus in these areas. You don’t want to see it combining things.”
Hickey contrasts ‘easy’ with ‘simple’. For ‘easy’, the central idea is proximity – in terms of access (e.g. already having something be installed, being able to easily install something), in terms of existing skills and capabilities, and so on. Hickey points out that ‘easy’ is subjective, because it is relative to the person making the judgement.
As one example here, Hickey states that the parentheses in Clojure are hard (i.e. the opposite of easy) but simple, and that
it is users’ responsibility
to fix this.
On the other hand, Hickey states that this notion of simplicity is objective, “we can probably go and look and see, I don’t see any connections, I don’t see where this twists with something else.”
Hickey stresses the difference between simplicity and low cardinality (“But not: One instance, one operation.”). He points out that the important thing is “lack of interleaving, not cardinality.”
Hickey sums up his argument against complexity as follows:
“We can only hope to make reliable those things we can understand”
“We can only consider a few things at a time”
“Intertwined things must be considered together”
“Complexity undermines understanding”
According to Hickey, simplicity has the following benefits:
Ease of understanding
Ease of change
Easier debugging
Flexibility
In terms of examples, Hickey has a few slides in his presentation
with some tables. The table below is a more condensed representation
of Hickey’s tables:
I may have misunderstood something; corrections welcome.
Complexity
Complects
Simpler alternative
State, objects
Everything that touches it
Values
Objects
State, identity, value
Values
Methods
Function and state, namespaces
Functions, namespaces
Variables
Value, time
Managed refs
Inheritance
Types
Polymorphism a la carte
Switch/matching
Multiple who/what pairs
Polymorphism a la carte
Syntax
Meaning, order
Data
Imperative loops, fold
what/how
Set functions
Actors
what/who
Queues
Variables
Value, time
Values
ORM
OMG
Declarative data manipulation
Conditionals
Why, rest of program
Rules
As one example, Hickey points out that “having state in your program is never simple”
and “The only time you can really get rid of it,
is it you present a functional interface on the outside,
a true functional interface, same input, same output.”
Hickey contrasts the words “complect” (to intertwine, interleave, braid)
and “compose” (to place together).
Ousterhout complexity
According to Ousterhout, “Complexity is anything related to the structure
of a software system that makes it hard to understand
and modify the system.” (Sec 2.1)
A closely related aspect is obviousness;
a system is considered to be obvious if
“a developer can quickly understand how the existing code works
and what is required to make a change”
and they “can make a quick guess about what to do,
without thinking very hard,
and yet be confident that the guess is correct” (Sec 2.2)
as well as “their first guesses about the behavior or
meaning of the code will be correct” (Ch. 18)
Ousterhout points out that obviousness is one
of the most important goals for system design;
and that obviousness is the opposite of high cognitive load
and unknown unknowns (see definitions below).
In Chapter 18, Ousterhout emphasizes the obviousness
is “in the mind of the reader” and that
“If someone reading your code says it’s not obvious,
then it’s not obvious, no matter how clear it may seem to you.”
“Complexity is caused by two things: dependencies and obscurity” (Sec 2.3) which are defined as:
“A dependency exists when a given piece of code cannot be understood and modified in isolation; the code relates in some way to other code, and the other code must be considered and/or modified if the given code is changed”.

data.title: Waymo rides cost more than Uber or Lyft and people are paying anyway
data.author: achristmascarl
data.article_summary: Obi应用的一项研究对比了Waymo自动驾驶汽车与Uber、Lyft在旧金山的打车价格和等待时间。数据显示，Waymo的平均价格为20.43美元，显著高于Lyft的14.44美元和Uber的15.58美元。尤其是在高峰时段，Waymo的平均价格比Lyft高出约11美元，比Uber高出近9.5美元。研究还发现，Waymo的短途行程相对更贵，且等待时间较长时，费用也会增加。尽管价格较高，70%的受访者表示更喜欢无人驾驶汽车，但74%的乘客仍对安全性表示担忧，且大多数人希望有远程人工监控。尽管Waymo价格较高，但消费者对其技术和新颖性表现出较大热情。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Waymo与Uber/Lyft等传统打车服务的对比，重点讨论乘坐体验、安全性、价格、技术先进性等方面。

不同观点：
• 支持Waymo的观点：
  - Waymo提供一致的、无变数的体验，车辆干净、驾驶平稳（[tempestn], [habosa], [pkrecker]）。
  - Waymo让乘客拥有更多的控制权，如播放音乐、调节音量、甚至上网工作，而不必担心打扰司机（[pkrecker], [Jelthi]）。
  - Waymo没有与司机的互动，避免了不必要的社交压力或不愉快的对话（[Jelthi], [greybox]）。
  - 安全性更高，用户更信任Waymo的自动驾驶技术，而不信任一些Uber司机的驾驶技术（[tempestn], [rossdavidh], [dawnerd]）。
  - Waymo的车辆为高品质车型，乘坐体验更好（[habosa], [Jelthi]）。
  
• 支持传统打车服务的观点：
  - 有些人，如东京的用户，认为当地的传统出租车服务已经非常专业，没有遇到过类似的不良体验，因此对Waymo的需求不大（[franciscop]）。
  - Waymo的价格可能更高，尤其对于一些身高较高的人来说，进出某些车型可能不太方便（[iwanttocomment]）。
  - 一些用户认为Uber/Lyft的价格在选择普通车型时更便宜，而Waymo的高品质服务对应更高的价格（[killion]）。

• 对技术和社会影响的讨论：
  - 有人担忧人们愿意为避免与他人互动而支付更多费用，反映出社会中对人际互动的排斥，并对AI技术的发展感到悲观（[oytis], [greybox]）。
  - 技术先进性和规模化生产将使Waymo的成本逐渐降低，未来其价格可能更具竞争力（[Animats]）。

• 对性别安全的关注：
  - 有欧洲女性指出，女性乘客可能更愿意支付额外费用以避免潜在的骚扰风险，这种安全需求也是选择Waymo的一个因素（[somewhatrandom9]）。

补充讨论：
• Waymo和Uber/Lyft的价格比较存在争议，一些人认为Waymo更贵，但也有用户指出，考虑到小费和车型质量，Waymo实际上更具性价比（[killion], [habosa]）。
• 用户对乘坐体验的期望因地域而异，东京的用户认为当地出租车服务已经非常优质，而在其他地区，用户对Waymo的无司机体验表现出更大兴趣（[franciscop], [harmmonica]）。
• 对未来AI技术在交通领域的应用及其对社会互动的影响，部分用户表示担忧（[oytis], [greybox]）。

A central premise of robotaxis is that high usage and lower labor costs will ultimately make it a cheap transportation option. That is still far from true, but now there’s some data that gives us an idea of by how much.
Obi, an app that aggregates real-time pricing and pick-up times across multiple ride-hailing services, has just published what it’s calling the “
first in-depth examination of Waymo’s pricing strategy.
” The company found Waymo’s self-driving car rides to be consistently more expensive than comparative offerings from Uber and Lyft — and it doesn’t seem to matter.
The report, shared exclusively with TechCrunch, is based on a month’s worth of data collected between March 25 and April 25 in San Francisco, California. Obi pulled nearly 90,000 “offer records” from Waymo, Lyft’s “standard” offering, and UberX in order to compare price and ETA. It then compared ride requests from the same times and routes. Obi found Lyft offered the lowest average price at $14.44. Uber was next at $15.58. Waymo’s average price across the month’s worth of data was $20.43.
Image Credits:
Obi
Ashwini Anburajan, Obi’s chief revenue officer, told TechCrunch this was somewhat surprising given the early popularity of Waymo’s service. Waymo said in May it’s providing 250,000
paid trips per week
across its first four cities. Higher pricing has apparently not dimmed that excitement.
“Colloquially, there is an idea that autonomous vehicles are something that will erode driver jobs and put drivers at risk. And I think the irony of what we’ve seen is that it’s actually quite expensive to run an AV, and that that’s not going to be happening, at least in the near term,” she said.
At peak hours, Obi found Waymo’s average price to be about $11 more expensive than a Lyft and nearly $9.50 pricier than an Uber.
“I didn’t expect consumers being willing to pay up to $10 more,” Anburajan said. “I think [that] speaks to a real sense of excitement for technology, novelty, and a real preference to sometimes be in the car without a driver.”

Obi found that not only was Waymo more expensive, but there was greater variability in its pricing than with Uber or Lyft.
Anburajan said one explanation is that Waymo’s pricing model is not as sophisticated. Uber and Lyft, she said, have had more than a decade to refine how they price rides. Those platforms are also a bit more dynamic, with drivers clocking in and out on their own time, or joining or abandoning the gig work altogether.
Waymo, meanwhile, has a mostly fixed but slowly growing supply of vehicles (though the pace of that growth
may soon accelerate
). This has led to what Anburajan said is more of a “pure supply and demand” pricing scheme.
That has two big impacts on customers. One is that short trips tend to cost more than longer ones. Obi found that Waymo rides cost roughly $26 per kilometer if the ride stays under 1.4 km.
This was true of the Uber and Lyft rides, too. But Obi found the shortest Waymo rides were priced 41.48% and 31.12% higher than Uber and Lyft, respectively. That gap shrunk as the rides got longer. In rides lasting between 4.3 km and 9.3 km, a Lyft cost $2.60 per km, an Uber cost $2.90 per km, and a Waymo cost $3.50 per km.
Image Credits:
Obi
The other impact is that longer wait times equals more expensive trips. After all, sending a car a long way to pick up a customer means it will perform fewer high-margin, short-distance rides.
That still isn’t discouraging Waymo customers, Anburajan said, even though Obi found Waymo to have a higher variability in wait times.
In addition to the data-based deep dive, Obi also surveyed riders in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, Arizona to get a better understanding of what might be driving these trends.
The company found that 70% of users who had taken a Waymo ride said they preferred a driverless car to a traditional rideshare or taxi.
Despite that enthusiasm, Obi found that safety is still a big concern for riders. Of those surveyed, 74% said safety is their biggest concern about robotaxis. Nearly 70% of respondents said they think there should be some form of remote human monitoring of the rides (something that is already a common practice).

  - 安全性更高，用户更信任Waymo的自动驾驶技术，而不信任一些Uber司机的驾驶技术（[tempestn], [rossdavidh], [dawnerd]）。
  - Waymo的车辆为高品质车型，乘坐体验更好（[habosa], [Jelthi]）。
  
• 支持传统打车服务的观点：
  - 有些人，如东京的用户，认为当地的传统出租车服务已经非常专业，没有遇到过类似的不良体验，因此对Waymo的需求不大（[franciscop]）。
  - Waymo的价格可能更高，尤其对于一些身高较高的人来说，进出某些车型可能不太方便（[iwanttocomment]）。
  - 一些用户认为Uber/Lyft的价格在选择普通车型时更便宜，而Waymo的高品质服务对应更高的价格（[killion]）。

• 对技术和社会影响的讨论：
  - 有人担忧人们愿意为避免与他人互动而支付更多费用，反映出社会中对人际互动的排斥，并对AI技术的发展感到悲观（[oytis], [greybox]）。
  - 技术先进性和规模化生产将使Waymo的成本逐渐降低，未来其价格可能更具竞争力（[Animats]）。

• 对性别安全的关注：
  - 有欧洲女性指出，女性乘客可能更愿意支付额外费用以避免潜在的骚扰风险，这种安全需求也是选择Waymo的一个因素（[somewhatrandom9]）。

补充讨论：
• Waymo和Uber/Lyft的价格比较存在争议，一些人认为Waymo更贵，但也有用户指出，考虑到小费和车型质量，Waymo实际上更具性价比（[killion], [habosa]）。
• 用户对乘坐体验的期望因地域而异，东京的用户认为当地出租车服务已经非常优质，而在其他地区，用户对Waymo的无司机体验表现出更大兴趣（[franciscop], [harmmonica]）。
• 对未来AI技术在交通领域的应用及其对社会互动的影响，部分用户表示担忧（[oytis], [greybox]）。

GNOME and Red Hat Linux Eleven Years Ago
By
Oscar Laycock
Four years ago, I switched on an old PC and found a seven year old (at
that time) copy of Linux on it. I still use parts of the 1998 Red Hat
Linux, today.
Red Hat Linux in 1998
My copy of Red Hat Linux is 5.1, codenamed "Manhattan". It was released
on May 22, 1998. The first Red Hat Linux 1.0 was released on November 3,
1994. Finally, Red Hat Linux merged with Fedora on 22 September 2003,
when Red Hat started Red Hat Enterprise Linux. I bought an official
boxed set with a manual in the autumn of 1998, for £29.95 (British
Pounds), from a mail-order catalogue. The catalogue also listed Slackware
3.5, Debian 1.3, TurboLinux 2.0, Caldera 1.2, FreeBSD 2.2.7, and BSD
Lite 4.4. Before then, I had been using
Coherent
,
a Unix Version 7 clone, originally produced for the PDP-11 in 1980 and
ported to the IBM PC in 1983.
The kernel is 2.0.34. It does not support thread-local storage, so I get
an error when I run a program built with a recent compiler.
Red Hat Linux 5.1 includes a "Linux Applications CD", a collection of
third-party programs. It has versions of
WordPerfect
[1]
, Tripwire, and
several relational databases.
Free software in 1998
Netscape
released
the source code of its browser and Communicator suite on March 31, 1998.
The GNU C Library, glibc, for my Red Hat 5.1 is version 2.0.7. Red Hat
Linux 4.2, released in May 1997, was the last Red Hat Linux based on the
Linux libc "libc 5". The Linux kernel developers had forked glibc in the
early 1990's. Their last version was called libc.so.5. According to
Wikipedia
, "when FSF
released glibc 2.0 in 1996, it had a much more complete POSIX standards
support, better internationalisation/multilingual support, support for
IPv6, 64-bit data access, support for multithreaded applications, future
versions compatibility support, and the code was more portable. At this
point, the Linux kernel developers discontinued their fork and returned
to using FSF's glibc." The new glibc 2.x series was given the internal
name "libc.so.6".
It was the time of the EGCS fork of the GNU C compiler. EGCS stood for
"Experimental/Enhanced GNU Compiler System". My Red Hat 5.1 includes an
early version, 1.0.2, released on March 18, 1998. But the default
compiler is gcc for stability.  GCC development followed a "cathedral"
model and had become quite conservative. In 1997, a group of developers,
some from Cygnus, formed EGCS to merge several forks, including g77
(Fortran), Pentium optimizations and many C++ improvements. According to
Wikipedia
,
"EGCS development proved considerably more vigorous than GCC
development, so much so that the FSF officially halted development on
their GCC 2.x compiler, 'blessed' EGCS as the official version of GCC
and appointed the EGCS project as the GCC maintainers in April 1999." It
was at that time that GCC was renamed the "GNU Compiler Collection".
Red Hat 5.1 came with a 2.0.1 version of PHP/FI. Developer Rasmus
Lerdorf warned that it is "quickly going to be superseded by Version
3.0", citing "dramatic improvements".  PHP3 was released on June 19
1998.
Wikipedia
says, "Zeev Suraski and Andi Gutmans, two Israeli developers at the
Technion IIT, rewrote the parser in 1997 and formed the basis of PHP 3,
changing the language's name to the recursive initialism PHP: Hypertext
Preprocessor
[2]
... Suraski and
Gutmans then started a new rewrite of PHP's core, producing the Zend
Engine in 1999. They also founded Zend Technologies in Ramat Gan,
Israel."
KDE 1.0 was released on 12 July 1998. KDE was founded in 1996. In
November 1998, Qt became open source, dual-licensed under the open QPL
and a commercial license for proprietary development.
1998 GNOME beta
Red Hat 5.1 includes a preview of the GNOME desktop environment, a beta
release.  The release notes say, "It is the results of about 4 months of
feverish work by an Internet-based development team." GNOME development
was announced in August 1997. The first major GNOME release, version
1.0, was to be in March 1999.
The GNOME distribution's README file says: "It is indisputable that
Linux is a rock-solid server OS, but traditionally Linux has not catered
as much to the typical desktop user, who wants to write email, browse the
web, etc. The GNOME project aims to provide a desktop environment that
will be friendly to novice users, but at the same time provide the power
and flexibility that advanced users expect."
GNOME did not come with a window manager. You could just run the GNOME
panel from your .xinitrc file, as in:
panel &
background-properties --init &
keyboard-properties --init &
mouse-properties --init &
fvwm2 -f .fvwm2rc.gnome     # disable fvwm2 taskbar
The back

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浏览器中的DRM（数字版权管理）及相关隐私、安全问题

不同观点：
• [tgsovlerkhgsel] 提到在浏览器中设置了需要明确批准才能使用DRM，但发现一些网站无明显理由也会请求此权限，且这种现象是间歇性的，即便使用了广告和跟踪阻止工具也无法完全避免。该用户对原因感到困惑。

• [1vuio0pswjnm7] 认为现代浏览器过于复杂，难以控制，主张使用更简单的软件来满足用户需求。这样不仅可以减少被监视和干扰的可能性，还更容易进行审计和控制。

• [jwrallie] 指出DRM还被Signal用于隐私保护，特别是在Windows环境下，并引用了Hacker News上的相关讨论。

• [JCattheATM] 表示完全禁用了浏览器中的DRM，只有在绝对必要时才会使用虚拟机和VPN来处理。

• [shmerl] 认为网站请求DRM权限的现象并不令人惊讶，似乎对[tgsovlerkhgsel]提到的情况并不感到意外。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是DRM在保护版权和隐私的同时，也可能带来不必要的请求和潜在的隐私问题。
• 另一个讨论点是浏览器复杂性与用户控制之间的平衡，有观点认为简化软件可以减少安全隐患和干扰。
• 还提到了使用虚拟机和VPN等技术手段来绕过DRM限制的实际操作方法。

这些观点共同构成了关于浏览器中DRM及其相关隐私和安全问题的多角度讨论。

data.title: George Orwell's 1984 and How Power Manufactures Truth
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 乔治·奥威尔的《1984》在特朗普首次当选美国总统后再次成为畅销书。尽管特朗普的美国与《1984》中的极权社会表面上有很大不同，但该书对政治乌托邦的描绘在文化中影响深远。书中描绘的权力对真相的绝对控制，以及通过“新话”限制思想的语言操控，反映了现实中的“后真相”现象。作者科林·马歇尔指出，奥威尔通过在BBC的经历认识到信息作为政治武器的运用，这启发了书中“真理部”和“新话”的设定。如今，类似的思想操控和偏颇的语言使用在文化争论中依然普遍。奥威尔提醒人们警惕这种噩梦般的局面，避免其成为现实。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公众与领导之间的关系、真理与权力的关系、现代社会中的政治正确与言论控制

不同观点：
• Göring的观点：领导人通过操纵民意，可以轻易地让民众支持战争，无论国家政体如何。Gilbert则认为民主制度中，民众通过选举代表拥有一定的影响力，如美国只有国会可以宣战。
• Gathering6678认为有些“真理”更容易被制造，比如仇恨和战争比和平更容易被煽动。
• tho23iwlefdsfd指出西方文化中政治性深植于历史中，而“Indosphere”地区在历史上更为微妙。
• mc32对书籍被加上触发警告表示不满，认为这是对批评权威主义的经典书籍的讽刺。
• chiefalchemist认为真理是信任的函数，权力越大，越容易被操纵，尤其在确认偏误的影响下。
• farts_mckensy指出“权力制造真理”是一个陈词滥调，并以2008年经济衰退为例，说明即使权力精英能影响叙事，但最终真理会显现，并影响历史进程。
• vjvjvjvjghv认为将问题简化为特朗普的影响是令人失望的，指出左派也有自己的“新话”，如政治正确和DEI努力。
• aaron695认为文化战士用政治化的方式描述现实，指出“男人可以怀孕”等言论，并认为特朗普的支持者是在反抗这种现象。

补充讨论：
• Göring与Gilbert之间的对话揭示了关于民主制度下民众影响力的争议。
• 讨论中多次提及奥威尔的《1984》以及赫胥黎的《美丽新世界》，反映了对现代社会中言论控制和政治正确的担忧。
• 对特朗普现象的评价存在分歧，部分评论认为特朗普代表了对“政治正确”的反抗。
• 真理与权力之间的关系被广泛讨论，部分评论强调权力精英可能暂时影响真理，但最终真理会显现。

争议焦点：
• 公众在不同政体下对政策的影响力，尤其是民主制度中的代表性问题。
• 真理是否可以被权力制造和操控，以及最终是否会有“真理显现”的时刻。
• 现代社会中政治正确与言论自由之间的平衡。

Soon after the first elec­tion of Don­ald Trump to the pres­i­den­cy of the Unit­ed States, George Orwell’s
Nine­teen Eighty-Four
became a best­seller again
. Shoot­ing to the top of the Amer­i­can charts, the nov­el that inspired the term
“Orwellian”
passed Danielle Steel’s lat­est opus, the poet­ry of Rupi Kaur, the eleventh
Diary of a Wimpy Kid
book, and the mem­oir of an ambi­tious young man named J. D. Vance. But how much of its renewed pop­u­lar­i­ty owed to the rel­e­vance of a near­ly 70-year-old vision of shab­by, total­i­tar­i­an future Eng­land to twen­ty-first cen­tu­ry Amer­i­ca, and how much to the fact that, as far as influ­ence on pop­u­lar cul­ture’s image of polit­i­cal dystopia, no oth­er work of lit­er­a­ture comes close?
For all the myr­i­ad ways one can crit­i­cize his two admin­is­tra­tions, Trump’s Amer­i­ca bears lit­tle super­fi­cial resem­blance to Ocea­ni­a’s Airstrip One as ruled by The Par­ty. But it can hard­ly be a coin­ci­dence that this peri­od of his­to­ry has also seen the con­cept “post-truth” become a fix­ture in the zeit­geist.
There are many rea­sons not to want to live in the world Orwell imag­ines in
Nine­teen Eighty-Four
: the thor­ough bureau­cra­ti­za­tion, the lack of plea­sure, the unceas­ing sur­veil­lance and pro­pa­gan­da. But none of this is quite so intol­er­a­ble as what makes it all pos­si­ble: the rulers’ claim to absolute con­trol over the truth, a form of psy­cho­log­i­cal manip­u­la­tion hard­ly lim­it­ed to regimes we regard as evil.
As James Payne says in
his Great Books Explained video on
Nine­teen Eighty-Four
, Orwell worked for the BBC’s over­seas ser­vice dur­ing the war, and there received a trou­bling edu­ca­tion in the use of infor­ma­tion as a polit­i­cal weapon. The expe­ri­ence inspired the Min­istry of Truth, where the nov­el­’s pro­tag­o­nist Win­ston Smith spends his days re-writ­ing his­to­ry, and the dialect of
Newspeak
, a severe­ly reduced Eng­lish designed to nar­row its speak­ers’ range of thought. Orwell may have over­es­ti­mat­ed the degree to which lan­guage can be mod­i­fied from the top down, but as Payne reminds us, we now all hear cul­ture war­riors describe real­i­ty in high­ly slant­ed, polit­i­cal­ly-charged, and often
thought-ter­mi­nat­ing ways
all day long. Every­where we look, some­one is ready to tell us that two plus two make five; if only they were as obvi­ous about it as Big Broth­er.

44294629.article_summary: 乔治·奥威尔的《1984》在特朗普首次当选美国总统后再次成为畅销书。尽管特朗普的美国与《1984》中的极权社会表面上有很大不同，但该书对政治乌托邦的描绘在文化中影响深远。书中描绘的权力对真相的绝对控制，以及通过“新话”限制思想的语言操控，反映了现实中的“后真相”现象。作者科林·马歇尔指出，奥威尔通过在BBC的经历认识到信息作为政治武器的运用，这启发了书中“真理部”和“新话”的设定。如今，类似的思想操控和偏颇的语言使用在文化争论中依然普遍。奥威尔提醒人们警惕这种噩梦般的局面，避免其成为现实。

data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: 佛罗里达州在对抗入侵的缅甸蟒蛇方面取得了重大进展。自2013年以来，西南佛罗里达自然保护组织已在200平方英里的区域内捕获并人道处理了20吨蟒蛇，仅在最近繁殖季就处理了6,300磅。这些蟒蛇对大沼泽地的生态系统构成威胁，捕食85种鸟类、哺乳动物和爬行动物，可能导致本地物种数量减少。研究人员利用技术，如给40条雄性蟒蛇安装追踪器，以找到并处理繁殖期的雌蛇，成功阻止了超过20,000颗蟒蛇卵的孵化。尽管蟒蛇仍在扩展活动范围，但长期监测显示这些措施正产生积极效果。
